Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + perf expectations — bench results attached

Hi Samira / Karthik — attaching the benchmark CSV and populating the MAP. Summary of the run (test harness: redwood-load v0.9, 1000 sample prompts from Acme transcript set, 30 runs per concurrency point):

Test environment:
- Dedicated GPU instance: A100-80GB equivalent (single card per worker)
- Model: redwood/open-6b-quant (v1) with standard KV cache enabled
- Network: 1Gbps test VLAN, <1ms intra-region fabric

TTFT (ms, end-to-end):
- Concurrency 1: p50=115 ms, p95=260 ms, p99=510 ms
- Concurrency 4: p50=130 ms, p95=290 ms, p99=620 ms
- Concurrency 8: p50=180 ms, p95=430 ms, p99=980 ms
- Concurrency 16: p50=370 ms, p95=890 ms, p99=2250 ms

Streaming latency per token (ms):
- Aggregated across prompts (tokenized): p50=45 ms, p95=110 ms, p99=240 ms

Throughput (tokens/sec aggregate):
- Concurrency 1: 1,250 t/s
- Concurrency 4: 4,600 t/s
- Concurrency 8: 8,400 t/s
- Concurrency 16: 11,200 t/s (note: diminishing returns due to context-saturation and scheduling overhead)

Observations and recommendations:
- With your target of ~8 concurrent active chat users, p95 TTFT ~430 ms — slightly above your stated 400ms threshold. We see that enabling per-customer prefix caching reduces p95 TTFT at concurrency 8 to ~320 ms in our smoke runs (we can enable in Dedicated).
- Batching set to max_batch=8 yields a throughput gain ~+30% but increases TTFT tail at high concurrency; recommend adaptive batching (cap on max_wait_ms) for best tail control.
- Quantization (current setup) gives good throughput; if you require lower tails under 400ms at 16 concurrency, we recommend moving to a 2-worker per-pod layout with dedicated KV cache replication (trade: +cost).

Attached: bench_results_acme_2026-10-20.csv, populated MAP document. I'll also upload a short capture showing the request->first token path: capture-demo-ttft.mp4

Action items populated in MAP:
- Redwood to enable per-customer prefix caching in Dedicated trial (ETA: 2 business days) — owner: priyom
- Acme to confirm final PO and target close date (ideal: 2026-11-10) — owner: Samira
- Joint smoke run after caching enabled — schedule: within 3 business days of PO

Cheers,
Priyom
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the thorough run. A few quick clarifications from procurement: 

- PO timeline: procurement can issue PO by 2026-11-12 provided we have the performance sweep with caching enabled and a short formal acceptance criterion in the MAP.
- Acceptance criterion suggestion: p95 TTFT <= 400ms at 8 concurrent active users with caching enabled, and no p99 spikes > 1s more than 3% of the time in a 1,000-sample window.

Can your team confirm we can meet that with the caching change + the adaptive batching recommendation? If so, we will target 11/12 PO and go-live by 11/30. Samira
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP finalization + confirmation on timeline

Samira — quick update from ops after the caching config change and a shorter adaptive-batching window were applied in the Dedicated trial yesterday: 

Validation run summary (smoke, 1,000 samples, concurrency 8):
- TTFT: p50=140 ms, p95=310 ms, p99=680 ms
- Streaming token latency: p50=48 ms, p95=95 ms, p99=210 ms
- Observed qps/tokens/sec: 8,250 t/s
- p99 spike rate (>1s): 0.9% in the 1,000-sample window (meets your <3% requirement)

Conclusion: With per-customer prefix caching + adaptive batching (max_wait_ms=8ms, max_batch=8) we meet the acceptance criteria you proposed. Ops recommends a 2-week probation window post-PO to monitor for any production tail regressions (standard for Dedicated).

Next steps (per MAP):
- Procurement PO submitted by 2026-11-12 (Acme)
- Redwood enables production config and schedule cutover: target 2026-11-20
- 2-week probation/monitoring: 2026-11-20 -> 2026-12-04

If this aligns, Karthik — please prepare the final MAP with the acceptance items and send the redline-friendly DocuSign link for signature.

—Rishi
